headline: A short-term funding extension that keeps federal agencies running at current spending levels and prevents a government shutdown when funding was set to expire on December 11, 2015.
what_it_does: Federal funding under the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2016 was set to run out on December 11, 2015. This bill extends that funding at the current annual rate until midnight on December 16, 2015, or until Congress enacts full FY2016 spending legislation, whichever comes first. The bill is designed to keep federal agencies open without a lapse in funding.

who_it_affects.group: Federal government employees whose agencies rely on annual appropriations
who_it_affects.how: Their agencies can keep operating and paying staff at current funding levels instead of facing a funding lapse on December 11, 2015.
Services funded through these agencies can continue without interruption during the extension period.
Work funded under federal agency budgets can continue at current funding rates while the extension is in effect.

when_it_takes_effect: Upon enactment on December 11, 2015, and the extension runs until the earlier of midnight on December 16, 2015, or enactment of FY2016 appropriations legislation.
